server: events (task 47-4a) — one EventBus per open project session (canvas/events.py), streamed as Server-Sent Events. Same server as v1.json (hub, /v1/p/<name>/…) and the stand-alone helper (helper.py, /api/events). Replayed in-process by test_protocol_events.py on a temp HD_HOME with a fake build (switches in `build` steps below are test-only).
auth: Session token or hub token (as v1.json), sent as X-HD-Token OR as ?hd=<token> (EventSource cannot set headers). Host must be 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port>. Failures are JSON like every route: 403 {error} (token/Host), 404 {error} (project not open), 503 {error} (too many streams on this project, 16).
stream: 200 text/event-stream; charset=utf-8, Cache-Control no-store, no Content-Length, connection closes when either side stops. The first frame is `retry: 2000` (EventSource reconnect delay). Each event is one frame: `id: <id>` `event: <type>` `data: <the whole event as one JSON line>` then a blank line. A heartbeat comment `: hb` is sent after 15 s without a frame. A client that disconnects is dropped within about a second (the server peeks the socket every second) — no thread is left behind.
resume: Last-Event-ID header (EventSource sends it on reconnect), else ?since=<id>. None = live only (no replay). Equal to the newest id = nothing to replay. Inside the ring (the last 256 events, or older by exactly one) = replay every event after it, then live. Older than the ring, larger than the newest id, or not an integer = one `reset` frame first (id = the newest id, data {type:'reset', reason:'too-old'|'unknown', last}) — refetch state (GET /api/state, /api/files) and go on from there. A stream that falls 512 events behind is closed; reconnect with Last-Event-ID.
ids: Integer, +1 per event, per project. The first id of a session is the clock in ms when the session opened, so a new session of the same project always has larger ids than an old one (an id from an old session = reset too-old, never mixed).
async_apply: POST /api/apply with "async": true (exactly the JSON value true; anything else = today's synchronous apply, unchanged). The server writes the source files, answers at once {accepted, failed, stamp, changed, paths, rev, async:true} and rebuilds in the background: one build at a time, writes that arrive while a build runs (or within 0.1 s of each other) are coalesced into the next build, and a build that new writes overtook is not announced (latest wins). Success = build.done listing every stamp and edit id it covers. Failure = every write not yet built is undone from its .hd-history stamp (newest first), the canvas is rebuilt from the undone sources, then build.failed {reason, reverted:[edit ids], kept:[edit ids that could not be undone because the file changed since], stamps, screens, repaired}. `rev` in the answer = the id of the screen.written event for this write — subscribe with Last-Event-ID = rev - 1 (or any id before it) to be sure to see its build event.

screen.written.doc: screen source files changed. by 'human' = written by this server (apply, delete, restore; sync = after the rebuild, async = before it). by 'ai' = the 1 s file watch saw a file change that this server did not write (agent, editor). rev = the /api/files seq at that moment (poll fallback: GET /api/files?since=rev). stamp = the .hd-history stamp that undoes this write (POST /api/restore), null for ai and for a restore without keep.

notes.changed.doc: .hd-canvas.json got a new rev by PUT /api/state or POST /api/reply (claim and release have their own events, also with rev).

release.doc: POST /api/release removed a cover (no event when nothing was held).

ai.write.doc: 48c AI undo row: act 'record' = a new row 'AI 반영 · <screen>' (GET /api/ai-writes seq), 'update' = the same row's restore point moved (the AI wrote again).

build.started.doc: async apply only: a background build starts for these writes.

build.done.doc: async apply only: the canvas is rebuilt with these writes (the newest build that no later write overtook).

build.failed.doc: the rebuild failed. async: the listed writes were undone (reverted = their edit ids), repaired = the rebuild after the undo succeeded. sync apply/delete/restore whose rebuild failed (already undone by the request itself) also publish it, with stamps [] and repaired null (the request undid and rebuilt by itself).

reset.doc: per stream, not stored: the Last-Event-ID was not usable. id = the newest id.

cases.name: Last-Event-ID in the future = reset unknown
Last-Event-ID not a number = reset unknown

flows.doc: Scripted scenarios replayed in order on a fresh session each (proj-c, hdfix out: screens home, list; state rev 3). Steps: open = start a stream (name, request as a case); send = one request + expect (+ save, as v1.json); events = read the next frames of that stream, they must be exactly these types in this order, each checked against `event` + its `types` shape + the extra shape given; build = test-only switch of the fake build: 'ok' | 'fail-once' (the next build fails, the repair build after the undo passes) | 'slow' (every build takes 0.6 s); get = GET a file and check its body contains a text.

cases.name: state writes: PUT state, reply, claim, release
sync apply = screen.written after the build, no build events
async apply: answer, screen.written, build.started, build.done
rapid async writes coalesce, latest wins
async build fails: sources undone, build.failed lists the edit ids
sync apply whose build fails = build.failed (already undone by the request)
